spine.claim: First-level thinking equates great companies with great investments, failing to recognize that crowd consensus drives price beyond intrinsic value.
Markets are governed not by efficient predictability, but by an emotional pendulum swinging ceaselessly between euphoria and despair.
True risk is not academic volatility or beta, but the permanent loss of capital that peaks precisely when the herd believes risk has vanished.
Superior performance demands lonely contrarian discipline and an uncompromising margin of safety to survive adverse realities.
The most important thing is acknowledging what you cannot know, letting downside protection ensure that upside takes care of itself.
